patterns.title: Device failed to authenticate to Entra ID
patterns.summary: dsregcmd reports that the device could not authenticate to Entra ID{detail}. Without device authentication, sign-in, Conditional Access and Intune check-in can all fail.

remediation.action: Check the device object in Entra ID
remediation.detail: Look the device up by name and ID. A disabled or deleted device object is the usual reason for this message.
If the object is gone, remove the stale state and join again (Autopilot devices: re-import the hardware hash and reset).
Confirm the device is in the sync scope and has synchronised to Entra ID.

patterns.title: Device registration failed
patterns.summary: The last device registration attempt failed: {detail}.

remediation.detail: The code names the exact reason (see the code meaning in the finding if known).
Registration needs access to the Microsoft device registration endpoints and a correct clock.

patterns.title: Device is not Entra joined
patterns.summary: dsregcmd shows AzureAdJoined = NO. That is expected for an on-premises domain-only device, but not for an Intune or Autopilot managed one.

remediation.action: Confirm the join type you expect
remediation.detail: Entra joined, hybrid joined and registered devices look different here. Check DomainJoined and EnterpriseJoined alongside.

patterns.title: Device keys are not protected by the TPM
patterns.summary: The device keys are not TPM protected. Some join and Conditional Access scenarios require that.

remediation.detail: Confirm the TPM is present, enabled and ready.
